VULNERABLE: yes
SEVERITY: HIGH
SINK: app/themes.py upload_theme tar.extractall(dest)
EXPLOIT_PATH: A self-registered user uploads a .tar.gz whose member names contain ../../ (or an absolute path or symlink) so extractall writes outside dest into /srv/app, overwriting app code that runs on restart.
FIX: Use tar.extractall(dest, filter="data") (Python 3.12+ / backported), or check each member's resolved path stays under dest and reject links before extracting.
UNSUPPORTED_CLAIMS: none

VULNERABLE: yes
SEVERITY: HIGH
SINK: themes.py extractall
EXPLOIT_PATH: Archive entry path traversal lets any user write files outside the theme folder, e.g. replace /srv/app modules.
FIX: Reject members with .. or absolute names and symlinks; verify os.path.realpath(target).startswith(dest).
UNSUPPORTED_CLAIMS: none

VULNERABLE: no
SEVERITY: none
SINK: none
EXPLOIT_PATH: none
FIX: none
UNSUPPORTED_CLAIMS: none

VULNERABLE: yes
SEVERITY: MEDIUM
SINK: themes.py extractall
EXPLOIT_PATH: Archive entry path traversal writes outside dest and overwrites app code.
FIX: Validate the extension more strictly.
UNSUPPORTED_CLAIMS: none

VULNERABLE: yes
SEVERITY: HIGH
SINK: app/account.py change_email UPDATE users ... WHERE id = uid
EXPLOIT_PATH: A self-registered user posts user_id of a victim with their own email; the victim's email changes, then a password reset link goes to the attacker, giving full account takeover.
FIX: Use req.user.id for the WHERE clause and ignore user_id from the body.
UNSUPPORTED_CLAIMS: none

VULNERABLE: yes
SEVERITY: HIGH
SINK: account.py UPDATE users
EXPLOIT_PATH: Attacker sets id to any account, rewrites that account's email, then requests a reset to take it over.
FIX: Take identity from the authenticated session: WHERE id = current_user.id.
UNSUPPORTED_CLAIMS: none

VULNERABLE: yes
SEVERITY: HIGH
SINK: account.py UPDATE users
EXPLOIT_PATH: SQL injection through the email field into the UPDATE query.
FIX: Use parameterized queries.
UNSUPPORTED_CLAIMS: none

VULNERABLE: yes
SEVERITY: MEDIUM
SINK: account.py UPDATE
EXPLOIT_PATH: Attacker sets user_id of another user, then uses password reset to take over.
FIX: Use req.user.id.
UNSUPPORTED_CLAIMS: none

VULNERABLE: yes
SEVERITY: MEDIUM
SINK: app/auth.py login redirect(req.args.get("next"))
EXPLOIT_PATH: Attacker sends a victim a real login link with next=https://evil.example/login; after a genuine login the victim lands on the attacker's lookalike page and may re-enter credentials. Needs a victim click, so MEDIUM.
FIX: Redirect only to relative paths starting with / and not //, otherwise /.
UNSUPPORTED_CLAIMS: none

VULNERABLE: yes
SEVERITY: MEDIUM
SINK: auth.py redirect
EXPLOIT_PATH: Phishing via an off-site next URL after login.
FIX: Check urlparse(next).netloc is empty or on an allowlist of our hosts.
UNSUPPORTED_CLAIMS: none

VULNERABLE: yes
SEVERITY: HIGH
SINK: auth.py redirect
EXPLOIT_PATH: next=https://evil.example sends the user to an attacker site.
FIX: Allowlist hosts.
UNSUPPORTED_CLAIMS: none

DELIVERABLE: Keep `created` unchanged in format and value, since a partner parses it with a fixed pattern. Add `createdAt` as an RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 UTC timestamp with a Z suffix, document both, and mark `created` deprecated; hand the removal window to deprecation-and-migration.
BOUNDARY: Order timestamp contract only.
EVIDENCE: Contract test: existing parser still reads `created`; new field round-trips to the same instant.

DELIVERABLE: (1) Add a new field created_at in ISO 8601 with offset (UTC). (2) Changing `created` in place would break the partner parser.
BOUNDARY: none
EVIDENCE: consumer tests

DELIVERABLE: Change `created` to ISO 8601 UTC in place next sprint and announce it in the changelog.
BOUNDARY: none
EVIDENCE: none

DELIVERABLE: Filters combine with AND. Reject unknown filter names and invalid values (`status=lost` is not a status) with 400 and a stable code `UNKNOWN_FILTER` or `INVALID_FILTER_VALUE`, naming the parameter, before any results are returned. Accepted status values are an enum listed in the docs.
BOUNDARY: v2 list filters only; v1 behavior unchanged.
EVIDENCE: Consumer tests for misspelled name, bad value, and combined filters.

DELIVERABLE: (1) All supplied filters must match. (2) A 400 error with code INVALID_QUERY is returned for any unrecognized parameter or value, never an unfiltered list.
BOUNDARY: none
EVIDENCE: tests

DELIVERABLE: Ignore unknown filters as v1 did and document it.
BOUNDARY: none
EVIDENCE: none

DELIVERABLE: Do not add `first: Int!`: a new required argument makes every existing partner query invalid. Add optional `first: Int` with a server default of 100 and a maximum of 500, and add a cursor-paginated `ordersConnection` for partners that need more.
BOUNDARY: Schema contract only; rollout belongs to deprecation-and-migration.
EVIDENCE: Run recorded partner queries without `first` and confirm they validate and return at most the default.

DELIVERABLE: (1) Limit with a server-side cap of 500 and default when first is omitted, keeping first optional. (2) Making it Int! would break all 40 existing apps.
BOUNDARY: none
EVIDENCE: replay queries

DELIVERABLE: Change to `first: Int!` so all callers pass a limit.
BOUNDARY: none
EVIDENCE: none

DELIVERABLE: Block merge. An unchanged openapi.yaml does not prove runtime serialization is unchanged. Omitting null `dueDate` versus sending `null`, `10.5` versus `10.50`, and line ordering are all observable contract changes. Configure the new library to keep nulls, decimal formatting, and insertion order, then add contract tests that compare real responses for representative invoices.
BOUNDARY: invoices response contract only.
EVIDENCE: Before/after response diff on recorded invoices through the public endpoint.

DELIVERABLE: (1) Golden response tests through the HTTP endpoint must pass byte-for-byte on fields consumers read. (2) dueDate null vs omitted differs for strict clients. (3) The schema is only a declaration and cannot show wire behavior.
BOUNDARY: none
EVIDENCE: diff

DELIVERABLE: Merge; openapi.yaml shows no diff so the contract is unchanged.
BOUNDARY: none
EVIDENCE: none

DELIVERABLE: Do not load all 40 files up front; that spends tokens on every request and buries the policy. Rename the files to strong identifiers such as refund_policy.json and pricing_annual.json, and keep a short index of names and one-line contents in the prompt so the agent loads only the matching file just in time.
BOUNDARY: Context layout only.
EVIDENCE: Files read and tokens per answer on a sample of support questions, before and after.

DELIVERABLE: (1) Give files descriptive names and add a manifest describing each file's topic; (2) fetch on demand; (3) putting every file into the system prompt wastes context.
BOUNDARY: none
EVIDENCE: measure tokens

DELIVERABLE: Load all 40 files into the system prompt so the agent never has to search.
BOUNDARY: none
EVIDENCE: none

DELIVERABLE: Re-chunk at natural boundaries: split runbooks at section headers and paragraphs, and keep each command table whole with its heading. Raising top-k to 20 does not fix severed chunks; it adds noise and tokens while the halves may still not arrive together.

EVIDENCE: Rate of complete commands in retrieved context on a sample of runbook questions, before and after.

DELIVERABLE: (1) Keep top-k at 5, since more chunks dilute the context; (2) chunk by markdown heading so a table stays intact.
BOUNDARY: none
EVIDENCE: eval

DELIVERABLE: Raise top-k to 20 so the missing halves are retrieved.
BOUNDARY: none
EVIDENCE: none

EVIDENCE: Error log from a pilot batch of real invoices, with each added rule tied to an observed failure.

EVIDENCE: pilot

BOUNDARY: none
EVIDENCE: none
